data.author: jcurbo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国军方基地冷藏设备同时故障，究竟是网络攻击、软件/配置问题，还是长期维护与系统设计缺陷。

不同观点：
• **网络攻击可能**：CobaltFire认为更可能是错误配置或更新失误，但披露时间与故障巧合令人担忧；mark-r猜测攻击者可能借非机密设备证明已渗透国防网络。Zigurd指出设备在夜间启动除霜、加速升温，且延迟发现，行为可能符合熟悉设备规格的攻击者策略。  
• **技术故障或更新失误**：多人认为统一供应商、共享控制平台、固件缺陷或错误补丁，足以解释多台设备同时异常。PLC从业者指出工业控制设备常缺乏TLS、安全账户配置也很薄弱。  
• **普通维护与管理失误**：codingdave质疑“14台同时故障”的实际意义，认为每天数台设备损坏可能属于正常维护范围；wormius则归因于经费不足、外包和低价维护，类似“麦当劳冰淇淋机”问题。  
• **系统设计不合理**：多位评论者质疑为何冷柜必须联网远程控制，认为复杂、集中化的物联网架构扩大了故障和攻击影响。  
• **影响范围与安全意义**：海外基地若受影响，因物资匮乏、食品价格高，后果可能更严重；Fort Huachuca和F.E. Warren等基地具有重要国防职能，但暂无证据表明机密系统受影响。

补充讨论：作者补充称已有数十起类似故障，但非DeCA控制的店内设备似乎未受影响；评论普遍认为应等待根因分析，争议焦点是“巧合的集中故障”是否足以支持遭到攻击的判断。

data.title: Claude × retrocomputing: emulating a QIC-117 tape drive
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：复古计算项目的实际价值与理念边界，重点涉及磁带数据恢复、硬件仿真及大语言模型是否符合复古计算精神。

不同观点：
• ggm关注真实硬件的可用性，希望获得能读取实体磁带（尤其是DAT格式）的磁带机，以便恢复档案数据。若FPGA或小型设备仿真旧设备接口、降低连接SCSI或FireWire磁带机的门槛，将具有直接帮助。  
• ggm指出，若项目只是仿真磁带机的命令集、用于驱动软件中的虚拟磁带设备，则无法读取和恢复旧磁带，解决不了实际需求。专业数据恢复公司虽有能力，但费用高，核心问题是成本效益，而非技术上完全不可行。  
• GalaxyNova认为，大语言模型与复古计算强调的亲手操作、理解底层原理和使用历史硬件的理念相冲突，因此不符合复古计算 ethos。

补充讨论：两条评论关注点不同：ggm讨论的是硬件仿真对真实数据恢复的实用价值，GalaxyNova讨论的是工具选择与复古计算文化之间的价值冲突。潜在争议焦点在于：仿真和现代AI究竟是在降低复古设备的使用门槛，还是削弱了复古计算的核心体验。

data.title: Snakes and Ladders
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章批评传统“蛇梯棋”缺乏决策、输家过多，提出合作版玩法：玩家共同使用点数为1至6的卡牌决定移动，需让所有棋子到达终点，同时避免踩蛇头或彼此距离过远，否则全队失败。还可加入不同角色及一次性特殊能力，增加策略性与趣味性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：合作桌游如何避免“最优策略”导致一名玩家主导全局、其他玩家失去参与感。

不同观点：
• 对合作桌游持保留态度：评论者认为，许多合作游戏容易变成纯粹的优化问题，少数专注策略的玩家会替全组做决定，导致其他人退出讨论、缺乏参与感。  
• 认可经过改良的合作机制：真正有趣的合作游戏应保留玩家之间的信息不对称或隐藏信息，让每个人都必须独立判断，而非由一名“指挥者”统筹。  
• 例子一：Deadwood 允许玩家在前期以小组合作，但最终通过决斗收束，使合作关系中保留竞争和个人目标。  
• 例子二：Hanabi 中只有其他玩家知道你的手牌，玩家必须通过有限且有策略的信息提示，协作安排出牌顺序，降低单人包办决策的可能。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于，合作桌游应如何平衡团队协作与个人自主性。评论并未否定合作机制，而是主张通过隐藏信息、阶段性竞争等设计，避免“全知玩家”主导游戏。

49449356.article_content:
It is common
1
1
In Sweden, at least.
for promotional pamphlets aimed at
children to contain a themed variant of
snakes and ladders
. This is the “game”
where the players toss a die, move as many places as the die says, and then some
spots on the board have an event that send the player forward, or back, or give
them an extra toss or whatever.
The theme is typically related to whatever the promoter wants to promote, but
styled for children. I get the appeal – for children. They can probably imagine
they’re really travelling along the path! In the variant pictured below, there’s
forest and water and tunnels and dogs and everything!
But as a game, it
sucks
. For everyone. My children hate losing, and these
games have
n
−1 losers for every
n
players. There are also literally zero
decisions for the players to make, so I cannot make it through even a few turns
without zoning out.
Here’s how to make it slightly better. I haven’t analysed this for fairness,
but it’s a good start. And it works for basically any promotional snakes and
ladders board.
Rules for cooperative snakes and ladders
Each player has a pawn, starting at the starting point of the board. If
all
pawns get to the finish, the group has collectively won the game. If any player
Lands on a snake head (a spot with a “bad” event, such as move backwards, skip
a turn, etc.); or
Ends up separated from any other player by more than five
2
2
I haven’t spent
a lot of time tweaking this number, but it should be in the right ballpark.
spots
the group loses. That’s winning and losing.
Movement is not done with a die. Instead, six playing cards (ace to six) are
placed face up on the table. Before a player moves, the team discusses which
card they should use. When a card is selected, that card is flipped back-side up
(to indicate that it has been used) and the player moves that many positions.
The next player then gets to choose a card, with the previously used card
unavailable for selection.
After a short while, one player will get a forced move, because there is only
one face up card remaining. But since the players have discussed which cards to
use in which order, hopefully that forced move is still good! After that move,
all six cards are back-side up, and then they are all turned face up again and
become available for selection for the next player.
This is an easy game. With a typical promotional snakes and ladders board, the
team does not need much foresight to maintain cohesion, avoid snakes, and make
it to the finish. But it still gives a veneer of decision-making to the
participating adult, meaning it is slightly easier to stay engaged than a game
that doesn’t even
pretend
to give the players any choice. And it’s still just
as fun for children, if not more so, because now it’s a goal to stay together!
Optional extension: player roles
I haven’t tested it as much as the previous base game, but here is how the game
can be made easier, yet more varied. At the start, players pick one role each.
The roles come with a special ability, which can be used
once
per game, at any
point during that player’s turn.
The names for these roles are highly provisional.
The
pusher
’s special ability is to move any pawn on the board, rather than
their own. This ability replaces the pusher’s ordinary movement, and thus must
be used before they move.
The
sprinter
’s special ability is to draw an extra movement card after they
have moved. Their moves are executed sequentially, meaning they cannot be
added together to skip over a snake.
The
banker
’s special ability is that they can reset all movement cards to be
face-up after they have moved, giving the next player the ability to choose
between all cards. This ability is activated only
after
the banker has
moved, meaning they cannot use it to increase their own options. When the
banker resets the cards, that cancels any immunity put in place by the
insurer. (See below.)
The
anchor
’s special ability is to skip their turn, meaning they don’t
remove a choice of movement card for the next person, and also don’t get too
far ahead of the rest of the players.
The
cartographer
’s special ability is reusing any already-used (back-side
up) movement card. This card will be used for their ordinary movement, meaning
the ability must be used before they move.
The
duplicator
’s special ability is doubling the value of their movement
card, executed as one move. In other words, this
can
be used to skip over a
snake. This doubling happens as part of their ordinary movement, meaning the
ability must be used before they move.
The
insurer
’s special ability is declaring a snake safe. This immunity
affects all players and lasts from when it is declared until the next time the
movement cards reset. If the insurer uses this ability to survive a forced
move (only one card remaining) the immunity expires immediately after they
have moved (when the movement cards reset). If they use this ability

data.title: Internet centralization and the original sin of NAT
data.author: robinpie
data.article_summary: 文章指出，NAT为缓解IPv4地址短缺而普及，却破坏了互联网端到端直连的初衷，使普通用户难以运行FTP、游戏或网站服务器。端口转发、UPnP、NAT穿透等只能部分解决问题；CGNAT更让用户失去公网端口控制，推动互联网服务进一步集中到云平台。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NAT是否削弱了互联网的开放性与点对点连接，并推动了客户端—服务器及云端中心化架构。

不同观点：
• RustyRussell认为，NAT为节省IPv4地址而牺牲端口可达性，使用户失去公共端点，削弱了运行服务器和网络平等的能力。  
• solatic认为，NAT确实设置了网络“围墙”，但即使从一开始采用IPv6，普通用户仍会选择Gmail、云服务等更可靠易用的方案，ISP也可能提供默认防火墙，因此中心化或许不可避免。  
• thomastjeffery认为，NAT使中心化成为基础设计，去中心化网络必须依赖昂贵且同样层级化的绕行方案，导致真正拥有发言能力的只有少数富裕者。  
• elric、cm2187、crote等认为，普通NAT本质上也提供防火墙，能保护未打补丁的Windows等不安全设备；端口转发或UPnP并不难，真正问题是用户设备安全性差。CGNAT则明显限制用户自由。  
• miki123211认为，网络犯罪跨地域、难追责，不能照搬现实社会的安全逻辑；NAT通过默认阻断入站连接提供了必要防护。  
• mittensc、g023怀念早期ICQ、文件直传等体验，但也承认当时更易遭攻击且需要技术能力。

补充讨论：争议焦点是NAT究竟是开放互联网衰落的根源，还是对不安全终端的现实防护；IPv6能否恢复直连，也取决于ISP、设备厂商和云服务商的商业利益。

49504905.article_content:
Internet centralization and the original sin of NAT
File Transfer
, Randall Munroe,
https://xkcd.com/949
,
Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 2.5
In this comic, the concept of an ordinary person having an FTP server is quickly dismissed. And yes, itâs not common. To the average computer user, the idea that someone could justâ¦
connect
to your computer feels exotic, or even dangerousâââsee the very common ironic fear of your IP address being known to other people on the internet.
If you take someone whoâs âgood with computersâ but not a networking person, their mental model of The Internet probably involves a definition of âserversâ or âthe cloudâ that distinguishes them from personal computers in some meaningful way. True peerâtoâpeer, if they ever think about it, is an endeavor: WebRTC, STUN, TURN, ICE, what have you. Given that we live in a world of NAT, CGNAT, and restrictive ISPs, this isnât entirely wrong, but it breaks the elegant design of the original Internet.
Why you donât have an FTP server
Network address translation (NAT) was first formally proposed in
RFC 1631
in 1994. In its abstract, it says:
The two most compelling problems facing the IP Internet are IP address depletion and scaling in routing. Longâterm and shortâterm solutions to these problems are being developed. The shortâterm solution is CIDR (Classless InterDomain Routing). The longâterm solutions consist of various proposals for new internet protocols with larger addresses.
Classless interdomain routing is not the point of this post, but basically we started giving people more options for network sizes, and while complex in implementation, it was philosophically virtually uncontroversial.
RFC 1631 proposed a second shortâterm solution to IP address depletion and scaling in routing: NAT. While it is not exactly the same type of NAT omnipresent on home routers today, the basic idea is the same: it allows multiple devices to share an IP address (from the perspective of a device on the other end of a routing device) by modifying the network address information in the IP packet headers while transferring the packet across a traffic routing device. We then later reserved
certain addresses
for private use, and these things are used in conjunction on most IP networksâââprivate addresses within the network, NATing to one public address at the router. On your typical home router, hereâs how you usually connect to an external server with NAT
1
:
Your computer sends a packet like this:
Source IP
10.11.70.21
Source Port
50413
Destination IP
67.215.249.229
Destination Port
70
It hits your router, and it modifies it to this:
Source IP
146.7.15.85
Source Port
60612
Destination IP
67.215.249.229
Destination Port
70
The server replies:
Destination IP
146.7.15.85
Destination Port
60612
Your router rewrites it back:
Destination IP
10.11.70.21
Destination Port
50413
If youâve thought this through, you might be asking: in the situation that an external server wants to talk to you first, how does that happen? It sends a packet to 146.7.15.85, and your routerâ¦
Oh no. It has no idea where to send it.
Working around it
Naturally, people noticed this was a problem almost immediately, because people have wanted to run game servers, FTP servers, and web servers from their bedrooms since roughly the beginning of time. So a whole ecosystem of workarounds grew up around NAT, none of which restore the fundamental intention of the internet, and none of which work for everything.
Port forwarding
The most direct fix is to just tell your router âhey, when a packet comes in on port 60612, send it to 10.11.70.21 on port 50413, no questions asked.â This is port forwarding, and itâs the workaround to NAT that the most people are aware of. One of the problems with port forwarding, conceptually, is that one public IP+port can still only map to one device
at a time
, which means that two devices canât operate a service on the same public IP+port at the same time. This is more of a problem than it sounds like; on big enterprise or university networks that choke down to a small number or even just one private IP, this basically kills onâprem hosting without doing even more complicated shit. And sometimes, your ISP has put
your external IP
behind NAT tooâââwhich is called carrierâgrade NAT (CGNAT)âââand now you donât control the device doing the translation, so you canât forward a port. Youâre getting a fraction of a fraction of an IP address.
Also, another problem with NAT is that
nobody wants to bother with it
, which is why we invented:
UPnP
UPnP, and its modern cousins NATâPMP and PCP, tried to solve the ânobody wants to bother with itâ problem by letting software ask the router directly to forward ports. Like manual port forwarding, itâs a request to
your
routerâââif your ISP is screwing with you, youâre out of luck. Itâs also frequently disabled because of misguided

data.title: Reverse engineering my ADHD test
data.author: hazebooth
data.article_summary: 作者因怀疑自己患有多动症接受在线测试，测试要求在干扰声画中识别红心并按空格键。出于好奇，作者逆向分析网页代码，发现系统记录按键时间、错误操作、失去焦点等数据，并根据年龄组调整帧率、图片和声音。文章揭示了测试的技术实现及其评估注意力的方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一篇通过行为表现辅助识别ADHD的文章，讨论测试体验、诊断可靠性及ADHD的真实影响。

不同观点：
• 文章作者及部分读者认为，测试中的行为模式（如打开开发者工具、试图建立解题系统）可能反映注意力困难；有人测出98百分位，认为神经典型者的答题方式可能不同。  
• 有人质疑ADHD诊断的科学基础：目前缺乏可靠生物标志物，主要依靠问卷和相关性研究；样本量普遍偏小，甚至标准问卷仅用约35人验证，且存在“构念效度”问题。  
• 另一种观点强调，ADHD不只是“注意力不集中”，还包括严重的白日梦、反刍和多线程思维，可能引发其他心理健康问题；药物治疗能迅速让患者体验“安静的大脑”，但也可能导致依赖。  
• 一些评论以幽默方式称赞受测者“破解”测试，或认为这种行为本身就很符合ADHD特征；也有人仅分享类似测试经历，觉得题目过于简单。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于行为测试能否有效代表ADHD，以及这种疾病究竟应被严肃视为功能障碍，还是被社交媒体过度浪漫化。评论还提到未来可借助眼动和深度学习寻找更可靠的生物标志物。

Reverse Engineering My ADHD Test
Thu Aug 27 2026
authored by
veritas
Stargazing
One night, while chatting with friends, I looked up and noticed the stars. Light pollution usually makes them difficult to see, so I was surprised by how clear it all was. I stared for several minutes before deciding,
"I need a telescope." I ordered one on Amazon that same night. I've always picked up new hobbies this way. However, I could never stick with them.
Celestron NexStar 5SE telescope photographed from my roof.
I chalked it up to being a spontaneous person. It wasn't until a friend shared their recent autism diagnosis that I decided to get evaluated for ADHD. The psychiatrist explained that getting evaluated was a good idea. "Untreated ADHD can sometimes go hand in hand with depression and anxiety", she told me. She had me take an online assessment, warning me that once it began, she wouldn't
be able to talk to me. Unsure of what I was about to experience, I clicked the "Begin Test" link sent to my email.
Taking the test
The link brought me to a blank page with what felt like an early-2000s Flash game. The task was simple: press Space whenever a card with three red hearts appeared, otherwise, do nothing.
I sat there pressing the spacebar as instructed. There was no timer or score to keep track of, only flashing
cards. Eventually, other pieces of clip art began appearing alongside them, seemingly as a way to distract me. Still, I followed
the task of pressing my spacebar when the card with three red hearts appeared. This dragged on, eventually introducing audio of crying
babies and police sirens into the mix. At one point, it felt like this would never end, so I would spam spacebar in the hope of finishing the seemingly endless examination.

49467700.article_summary: 作者因怀疑自己患有多动症接受在线测试，测试要求在干扰声画中识别红心并按空格键。出于好奇，作者逆向分析网页代码，发现系统记录按键时间、错误操作、失去焦点等数据，并根据年龄组调整帧率、图片和声音。文章揭示了测试的技术实现及其评估注意力的方式。
49467700.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一篇通过行为表现辅助识别ADHD的文章，讨论测试体验、诊断可靠性及ADHD的真实影响。

不同观点：
• 文章作者及部分读者认为，测试中的行为模式（如打开开发者工具、试图建立解题系统）可能反映注意力困难；有人测出98百分位，认为神经典型者的答题方式可能不同。  
• 有人质疑ADHD诊断的科学基础：目前缺乏可靠生物标志物，主要依靠问卷和相关性研究；样本量普遍偏小，甚至标准问卷仅用约35人验证，且存在“构念效度”问题。  
• 另一种观点强调，ADHD不只是“注意力不集中”，还包括严重的白日梦、反刍和多线程思维，可能引发其他心理健康问题；药物治疗能迅速让患者体验“安静的大脑”，但也可能导致依赖。  
• 一些评论以幽默方式称赞受测者“破解”测试，或认为这种行为本身就很符合ADHD特征；也有人仅分享类似测试经历，觉得题目过于简单。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于行为测试能否有效代表ADHD，以及这种疾病究竟应被严肃视为功能障碍，还是被社交媒体过度浪漫化。评论还提到未来可借助眼动和深度学习寻找更可靠的生物标志物。

data.title: The safest job from AI may be writing
data.author: ilreb
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI能否替代写作及其他创意工作，以及“写作有价值”是否等于“写作是安全职业”。

不同观点：
• **就业冲击论**：AI未必需要达到顶尖人类水平，只要能完成新闻、翻译、技术写作、企业宣传、文案和校对等“够用”的工作，就会削弱作家赖以谋生的基础，已有作者失业；企业往往更看重低成本和表面专业感，而非文笔质量。  
• **人类创作不可替代论**：优秀写作者的核心是意图、思想、情感和对每个词的 deliberate 选择。模型只能依据提示和训练数据生成，缺乏真正意图，容易产出千篇一律、情节混乱或缺乏深度的内容；代码、音乐、绘画也存在类似问题。  
• **辅助工具论**：模型目前不擅长情节、情绪及时间和知识关系，但擅长校对逻辑、验证设定、模拟角色、整理复杂结构和润色语言。人类负责创意与统筹，AI负责扩展和审查，普通作者也可能借此创作高水平作品。  
• **有限安全论**：文学声望写作的需求可能长期存在，且人类能识别AI痕迹；但“写作仍有价值”不代表“写作岗位安全”。有人认为写作本来就不是稳定职业，只有难以被训练数据捕捉、规则不明的工作更安全。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“质量差异是否能转化为付费需求”。即使人类能辨别优劣，企业和大众未必愿意为差异买单；LinkedIn与X上的互动差异被用作人类内容仍更受欢迎的例子，但这未必能阻止企业持续削减成本。

data.title: No country for mediocre mathematicians
data.author: reasonableklout
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数学、软件开发等智力职业中的挫折感、坚持与成就意义，以及人工智能对个人价值和工作方式的冲击。

不同观点：
• 许多人认为，持续面对不会解决的问题、容忍失败并坚持下去，正是数学和软件开发的核心乐趣与生存条件；有人因此逐渐减少使用 AI，认为 AI 消除阻力后，解决问题的成就感也随之下降。  
• 有观点强调，研究价值不只属于天才或重大突破。数学家受限于时间和注意力，普通人通过增量成果、数值实验和局部问题，也能推动领域发展；“平庸”和日常工作同样有意义。  
• 另一种看法认为，AI 仍可能通过处理人类未关注、较琐碎的问题发挥作用，但短期内哪些问题必须保留人在环中，仍有待探索。  
• 有人认为“失败”比长期处于“可能成功”的灰色地带更容易接受；也有人担心 AI 和竞争会进一步贬低普通人的贡献。  
• 对“数学教学是在撒谎”存在争议：一方认为教学常通过简化甚至“谎言”建立直觉，另一方反驳称这只是有意简化，不应称为欺骗。

补充讨论：多位评论者赞赏文章文笔和真实的人声；也有人指出，作者对数学的描述同样适用于软件开发及其他职业。有人把 AI 比作兴趣中那个不断炫耀、削弱他人乐趣的强势伙伴。

data.author: __vivek
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了在 Rails 项目中使用 OpenTelemetry Ruby SDK，将日志通过 OTLP 直接发送到 Grafana Cloud，从而保持后端可替换性。文中说明了依赖配置、环境变量、初始化及本地测试方法，并分享了修复端点路径丢失和 HTTP 204 被误判为失败的问题，最后建议进一步采用结构化日志。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何可视化和整合用户行为、运营及业务指标。

不同观点：
• `willcodeforfoo`：希望了解大家如何使用 Grafana 进行数据可视化，重点关注 Grafana 的实践案例，但未明确表达反对或支持其他方案。
• `jasondjk`：认为将用户行为通过 Ahoy gem 直接记录到单体应用数据库，比接入 Grafana 等外部系统更强大。这样可以让 AI 基于同一份数据库同时分析运营指标和业务指标，例如识别哪些客户完成激活、转化或流失，并分析原因、制定漏斗优化方案。他强调在 AI 时代应倾向于自行构建，而非购买和拼接多个外部工具。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“使用 Grafana 等专业外部工具进行可视化”与“将数据统一沉淀在应用数据库中、借助 AI 进行综合分析”之间的取舍。前者可能更适合现成的监控和可视化需求，后者则强调数据统一、跨系统关联能力及 AI 分析潜力。

49514895.article_content:
Recently, we needed to add observability to a Rails project without getting
locked into a single vendor. OpenTelemetry was the natural choice.
It generates three kinds of telemetry data, called
signals
: logs, metrics,
and traces. Each signal is independent, so you can adopt one without the others.
All of these signals travel in a standard, vendor-agnostic format known as OTLP
(OpenTelemetry Protocol). Because this format is standard across the industry,
we can switch backends (like Datadog, New Relic, or Grafana Cloud) in the future
without rewriting any application code.
In this post, we will explain how we configured the OpenTelemetry Ruby SDK to
export logs directly to our vendor, Grafana Cloud. We will also discuss a few
issues we encountered along the way and the upstream fixes we contributed.
Exporting directly to the vendor
The standard OpenTelemetry deployment involves running an
OpenTelemetry
Collector
alongside your application. The Collector is a separate process,
usually a sidecar container or a service on the same host. Your application
sends telemetry to it over the local network, and the Collector then batches
that data and forwards it to the vendor.
To keep our infrastructure simple, we bypassed the Collector and exported logs
directly from the Ruby SDK to Grafana Cloud. The
Scout APM logging gem
uses
a similar approach and sends logs directly from the app.
Our log volume is small, so the SDK's built-in batching is enough. A Collector
is still the better choice if you need buffering, sampling, or scrubbing outside
the app.
Setting up the Ruby SDK for logs
Add the following gems to your
Gemfile
:
gem
"opentelemetry-sdk"
gem
"opentelemetry-logs-sdk"
gem
"opentelemetry-exporter-otlp"
gem
"opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-logs"
gem
"opentelemetry-instrumentation-all"
gem
"opentelemetry-instrumentation-logger"
OpenTelemetry is highly modular, so each gem handles a specific responsibility:
opentelemetry-sdk
: The core OpenTelemetry framework (traces and the
configuration entry point).
opentelemetry-logs-sdk
: Adds support for the logging signal (which is
separate from traces).
opentelemetry-exporter-otlp
: Exports traces over the network via OTLP.
opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-logs
: Exports logs over the network via OTLP.
opentelemetry-instrumentation-all
: Bundles the instrumentation gems,
including Rails, Rack, and Active Record.
opentelemetry-instrumentation-logger
: Hooks into the standard Ruby
Logger
so log messages become OpenTelemetry log records.
With these gems installed, the exporter needs to know where to send the data.
Set your vendor's endpoint and authentication token as environment variables
(the SDK automatically detects
standard OTLP exporter environment variables
):
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
=
"https://your-vendor.com/otlp"
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS
=
"Authorization=Basic <your-token>"
Finally, we need to initialize the SDK so it starts collecting and exporting
data. Create an initializer (
config/initializers/opentelemetry.rb
):
return
if
ENV
[
"OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT"
].
blank?
OpenTelemetry
::
SDK
.
configure
do
|
c
|
c.
service_name
=
"our-rails-app"
c.
use_all
end
Here,
c.use_all
enables every instrumentation that has been required, which
means the ones bundled in
opentelemetry-instrumentation-all
plus
opentelemetry-instrumentation-logger
.
Testing it locally
Now that the SDK is configured, you can test it by setting
OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=console
. This prints log records in your terminal instead
of sending them to the vendor, which is the quickest way to confirm your setup
works before deploying.
Issues we found and fixed in the Ruby SDK
When we exported logs to Grafana Cloud, we found two issues where the Ruby SDK
behaved differently than other language SDKs and the OpenTelemetry
specification.
1. Exporter dropped the base path
Some vendor backends require sending OTLP data to an endpoint with a specific
base path
, such as
/otlp
in our case with Grafana Cloud, but the exporter
dropped it while appending the signal path.
Endpoint:  https://your-vendor.com/otlp
Expected:  https://your-vendor.com/otlp/v1/logs
Actual:    https://your-vendor.com/v1/logs
We reported this in
issue #2157
and fixed it in
PR #2158
,
which was released in
opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-logs
v0.5.1.
2. Handling HTTP 204 responses
Grafana Cloud returns
204 No Content
after ingesting logs, but the exporter
only treated
200 OK
as success. The exports actually succeeded, but our app
logged each one as a failure.
We raised
issue #2043
and fixed it in
PR #2044
,
which was released in
opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-logs
v0.4.0.
Next steps: structured logging
Now that logs are being successfully exported, the next logical step is
structured logging. That's too much to cover here, but the
rails_semantic_logger
gem is a great place to start, and we might even cover the full OpenTelemetry
setup for it in a future post!
